info.name: Personal Budget API
info.description:
REST API for the Personal Budget app. Base URL: `{{baseUrl}}`.

**Quick start**
1. Import this collection and one environment (Production or Local) and select it.
2. Run **Auth > Register**, then **Auth > Log in**. The tokens are saved
   automatically; every other request sends `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}`.
3. Create a category, then a transaction. Create calls save the new id in
   `{{categoryId}}`, `{{transactionId}}`, ... so the next requests just work.

**Conventions**
- JSON in, JSON out: `Content-Type: application/json`, `Accept: application/json`.
- Money is a decimal **string** (`"450.00"`), never a float. Dates are
  `YYYY-MM-DD`; months are `YYYY-MM`.
- Access token lives 60 min; refresh token 7 days and **rotates** on every refresh.
- Errors: 400 `{"field": ["message"]}` (sometimes a bare array), 401/404/429
  `{"detail": "..."}`.

Full reference: the OpenAPI file (`docs/api/openapi.yaml`) and `/api/schema/swagger-ui/`.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Register, log in, refresh and revoke JWT tokens.

request.description:
Creates the account and seeds 49 default categories. `timezone` must be an IANA name (e.g. `Asia/Kolkata`, default `UTC`) and decides what "today" means for recurring entries. A taken email returns a generic 400 on purpose. Limited to 5 requests/minute per IP.

**Body:** JSON, see the example. Required fields are marked in the OpenAPI file.

**Responses:** `201`, `400`, `429`

Returns a short-lived `access` token (60 minutes) and a `refresh` token (7 days). Send `Authorization: Bearer <access>` on every other request. Limited to 5 requests/minute per IP.

**Body:** JSON, see the example. Required fields are marked in the OpenAPI file.

**Responses:** `200`, `400`, `401`, `429`

exec: // Rotation: the old refresh token is now revoked, keep the new one.

request.description:
Refresh tokens **rotate**: the response contains a NEW `refresh` token and the one you sent is revoked. Always store the new one. A 401 here means the user must log in again.

**Body:** JSON, see the example. Required fields are marked in the OpenAPI file.

**Responses:** `200`, `400`, `401`

Revokes the refresh token. Discard both tokens on the device afterwards. No Authorization header is needed.
